lines.text: The floor tilts into a graph. A pose is three numbers: x, y, and theta, the heading.
This is the robot when photo two was taken, from the rewound wheel memory: x one, y zero point five, facing zero degrees.
The camera gives the tag in the robot's own frame: two ahead, zero point one left, turned one eighty to face us.
To chain them, we compose, written as a plus in a circle. Tag in the world equals robot, composed with tag in robot.
Composing has two steps. First, rotate the second arrow by the robot's heading. Our heading is zero, so nothing turns.
Second, add. One plus two is three. Zero point five plus zero point one is zero point six. Headings add to one eighty.
So photo two puts the tag at three, zero point six, facing us. The code will make exactly these numbers.
Why rotate? If the robot faced thirty degrees, ahead points another way. The arrow turns to one point six eight, one point zero nine.
Add, and the tag lands at two point six eight, one point five nine. Skip the rotation, and you'd be about a meter wrong.
Two more tools. The inverse, a small minus one, is the trip backwards. And seen from measures one pose from another.
